verses.text: “Run for your lives, children of Benjamin! Get out of the middle of Jerusalem! Blow the trumpet in Tekoa and raise a signal at Beth Haccherem. Disaster is looming from the north, and it’s going to leave a trail of destruction.
I’ll cut off Daughter Zion, lovely and delicate as she is.
Shepherds will come at her with their flocks. They’ll pitch tents all around her, each grazing his flock wherever he’s set up.”
“Get ready to go to war against her! Up you get! Let’s attack at noon. Oh no, the day’s getting away from us. Look how long those evening shadows are.
Get up! Let’s go after dark and tear down her palaces.”
The LORD of Armies said, “Chop down trees and pile up an attack ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city that has to answer for what she’s done. Oppression fills her from the inside.
She pumps out evil like a well pumps out water. You can hear violence and destruction in her streets. All I see before me is sickness and wounds, day after day.
Take the warning, Jerusalem, or I’ll pull away from you. I’ll leave you a wasteland, a place where nobody lives.”
The LORD of Armies says, “They’re going to pick clean what’s left of Israel like grapes on a vine. Go back over it, like a grape picker reaching again to fill the baskets.”
Who can I speak to and warn who’ll actually hear me? Look, their ears are uncircumcised. They can’t listen. They treat the LORD’s word like an insult. They get no joy from it.

So I’m full of the LORD’s anger, and I’m worn out from holding it in. “Pour it out on the children in the street and on the young men gathered together. Husband and wife will both be taken, the old and those who’ve lived to a very old age.
Their homes will go to other people, along with their fields and their wives. I’m stretching out my hand against the people who live in the land,” says the LORD.
“From the least important to the most powerful, everybody’s hungry for what they can grab. From prophet to priest, everybody’s dealing crooked.
They’ve barely touched my people’s wound and called it healed. ‘Peace, peace!’ they say, when there’s no peace at all.

Did they feel ashamed after doing something so disgusting? They had no shame. They couldn’t even blush. So they’ll go down with the others who fall. When I come to hold them to account, they’ll be brought down,” says the LORD.
The LORD says, “Stop at the crossroads and look around. Ask where the old paths are. Ask, ‘Where’s the good road?’ Walk it and you’ll find rest deep down.” But they said, “We’re not walking it.”
I stationed watchmen over you and said, “Listen for the trumpet!” But they said, “We’re not listening!”
So listen, you nations. Everyone gathered, take note of what’s going on among them.
Listen, earth! I’m bringing disaster on these people, the fruit of their own plans. They didn’t listen to what I said, and they tossed my law aside.
What use do I have for frankincense from Sheba or fragrant cane from far away? Your burnt offerings aren’t acceptable, and your sacrifices don’t please me.”
So the LORD says, “Look, I’m putting stumbling blocks right in front of these people. Fathers and sons will trip over them together. Neighbor and friend will perish.”
The LORD says, “Look, people are coming from the north. A great nation is being stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.
They grip bows and spears. They’re cruel and show no mercy. They roar like the sea as they ride in on horses, each one lined up for battle against you, Daughter Zion.”
We’ve heard the news. Our hands have gone weak. Panic has a grip on us, and we’re hurting like a woman in labor.
Stay out of the fields and off the roads. The enemy’s sword is out there, and terror is closing in from every direction.
Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in the ashes. Cry bitterly, like someone mourning their only son. The destroyer will be on us before we know it.
“I’ve made you a metal tester and a fortress among my people so you can find out what their ways are made of and put them to the test.
Every one of them is deep in rebellion, going around spreading slander. They’re bronze and iron. They’re all corrupt in how they deal with people.
The bellows are blasting, and the lead burns away in the fire. The refining goes on for nothing because the wicked are still there.
People will call them rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.”
